A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GIOROM and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Their substantial overlap supports reliable comparison despite the methodological revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulator evaluations, reconstruction and rollout errors, baseline comparisons, timing measurements, and ablations across several physical systems.

after.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, including material benchmarks, kernel-ROM comparisons, and sparsity, reconstruction-failure, runtime, and memory analyses.

M1.justification: v2 reconstructs full fields using learned global basis functions and per-step least-squares coefficients (Section 3). v3 replaces this with a learned local kernel-ROM that reconstructs query values from neighboring sparse evaluations (Section 4; Algorithms 1–2). The stated time-stepper objective also drops the weighted position-error term in v2 Equation 10, retaining acceleration error in v3 Equation 8.

E1.justification: The principal material families and datasets remain. v3 adds evaluated elastic-collision and chocolate phase-transition scenarios in Figure 5, while the explicit 98K-point different-geometry test in v2 Table 2 is no longer reported. This changes particular test scenarios without broadly replacing the application coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds LiCROM and CROM to the ROM comparison alongside retained PCA/POD and autoencoders (Figure 2). GAT disappears from both accuracy and timing comparisons, and the FNO-based comparisons in v2 Tables 6–7 are removed. GNN/GNS is a retained comparator under revised naming; GINO, GNOT, and IPOT also remain.

E3.justification: The ROM comparison changes from shuffled-index reconstruction with reduced dimension 3 to dynamic-fluid rollout evaluation. New experiments introduce 30,000-step kernel-ROM training and systematic radius, sample-size, and MLP configurations; Figure 4 explicitly includes graph-construction overhead in timing and memory measurements. The shared five-million-step time-stepper budget and ten held-out validation sets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands the existing sparsity analysis with Water2D and Plasticine3D failure cases, extreme-sparsity Dragon reconstructions, and kernel-ROM cost sensitivities (Appendix J). It removes v2's component/noise ablations, radius–viscosity analysis, latent-grid study, and training-set-size and other hyperparameter sweeps. The message-passing-layer and FPS/Delaunay studies are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 explicitly reports three randomized-index retries for each reconstruction method. v3 removes that repeated-trial reporting without replacing it with seed counts, confidence intervals, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The retained ten validation sets do not establish repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1's accuracy values remain unchanged, but v3 adds fluid-ROM results, including MSE 0.0091 for GIOROM, 0.033 for LiCROM, and 0.079 for CROM (Figure 2), plus extensive sparsity and cost results. GNS Elasticity rollout MSE changes from 0.0019 to 0.0003 (v2 Table 7; v3 Table 3), reversing its ordering against the unchanged proposed result of 0.0004. Upscaling times are also revised for the changed reconstruction method (v2 Table 5; v3 Table 6).

T1.justification: v3 replaces the global-basis least-squares formulation with a local kernel estimator and its reconstruction objective. Appendix B adds RKHS assumptions, reproducing-kernel mathematics, and an exact-interpolant recovery assertion; Appendix J.4 develops the graph-network interpretation through Monte Carlo kernel integration. These are substantive mathematical additions beyond notation changes.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes a proposed graph neural-operator time-stepper combined with existing neural-field ROM techniques. v3 makes local kernel-based manifold parameterization a central novel contribution and claims advantages for dynamic fluid reconstruction. The broader claims of data-driven sparse simulation, discretization invariance, and 6.6–32-fold input reduction remain.

C2.justification: v3 expands the sparsity discussion into explanations involving lost physical structure, reconstruction clustering, and why increasing radius cannot recover missing information (Appendix J). It adds a local-kernel explanation for improved fluid interfaces and limitations concerning unbounded flows, fixed temporal discretization, integration schemes, and the selected time-stepper. The earlier out-of-distribution and discontinuity caveats are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds kernel-transform pseudocode, kernel MLP widths, training duration, fixed initial-state neighborhoods, and separate position/deformation inputs for non-fluid/fluid systems (Appendices C, E, and G). It also specifies NOT attention and branch/trunk settings. Conversely, v2's explicit six-step input window, normalization procedure, and noise specifications disappear; the code-access link remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantial kernel-ROM, data-driven ROM, and manifold/RKHS literature, including work by Honeine, Salvador and colleagues, Guo and Hesthaven, and Berry and Sauer. It positions the method against both global neural-field reconstruction and discretization-dependent kernel ROM. LiCROM and CROM were already cited in v2; their new experimental participation is separate from this positioning change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around kernel-ROM. v3 introduces a Definitions section, changes the order and emphasis of the method sections, merges discussion and conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices. These changes extend well beyond inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adds an overview comparison, ROM baseline visualizations, a forward-pass flowchart, and extensive cost and failure panels. Existing material illustrations are revised and relocated, while v2 Figure 4a is enlarged and reused as v3 Figure 19. Baseline and timing tables move largely into the appendix, several ablation displays disappear, and table structures and captions change.

improvement.justification: v3's CROM/LiCROM comparison and expanded sparsity/cost analyses make the empirical assessment more informative than v2's narrow shuffled-index ROM comparison. However, v3 removes explicit normalization/noise details and adds an exact-RKHS-recovery assertion (Appendix B.3) without establishing that its kernel-weighted sample values provide the required interpolation coefficients. The stronger empirical evidence and these theoretical and reproducibility gaps leave the net quality effect uncertain.
